headline: PM Tarique Rahman leaves for Tokyo on 4-day state visit to Japan
summary: The Prime Minister is leading a 15-member delegation to Japan at the invitation of Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has departed from Dhaka for Tokyo on a four-day state visit to Japan, accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman.
The Prime Minister left Shahjalal International Airport around 12:15 am on Monday via a commercial flight operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
He is visiting Japan at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and is leading a high-level 15-member delegation.
The delegation includes Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Advisor Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir.
Also accompanying the PM are State Minister for Power Aninda Islam Amit, Telecoms Advisor Rehan Asif Asad, and Bangladesh Bank Governor Mostaqur Rahman.
The delegation further includes BIDA Chairman Chowdhury Ashik Mahmud Bin Harun, Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam, and several senior government officials.
Political representatives including Azizul Haque Islamabadi of Hifazat e-Islam and Md Tarek Rahman of Amjanatar Dal are also part of the delegation.
Officials from the Prime Minister's Office, the Foreign Ministry, and the Special Security Force are accompanying the Prime Minister on this trip.

topic: deep depression in bay of bengal may turn into cyclone
headline_marked: Bay depression [[may develop into cyclone]] named Arnab
headline: Bay depression may develop into cyclone named Arnab
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department warns of a deep depression that could intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm heading toward India's coast.
details: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified and is expected to develop into a cyclone. If it forms, the storm will be named Arnab, a name proposed by Bangladesh meaning 'ocean' or 'sea'.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) forecasts that the system may intensify into a cyclone on Monday and potentially cross India's Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday.
As of Sunday noon, the depression was centered 810km south of Chattogram Port, 730km south of Cox's Bazar Port, 850km south of Mongla Port, and 780km south of Payra Port.
Highest sustained winds within 48km of the depression's center are reaching 50km per hour, with gusts or squalls of up to 60km per hour, causing rough seas near the center.
In response, Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been advised to hoist distant warning Signal No. 1.
All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern Bay of Bengal have been instructed to move closer to the coast and navigate with caution until further notice.
